case_assessment.summary: The graph captures the main toxic plume outcome and most downstream dispersion logic, but it is overly compressed at the front end of the scenario. The main causal weakness is that the initiating event is framed only as a hose misconnection rather than the actual incompatible transfer/mixing that generated the exothermic reaction and toxic release. The pressure node is also ambiguous and its link to dispersion is weak. In addition, the hazard consequence evidence does not follow the direct-quote requirement.
main_problems: Ev1 is too narrow and does not explicitly represent sulfuric acid being discharged into the sodium hypochlorite tank and mixing incompatibly.
C2 (Low pressure) is ambiguous for this scenario because the truck was pressurized for unloading while the tank vented atmospherically, and its edge to dispersion is weak.
H1 evidence is not a clean verbatim quote and should be replaced with direct quoted support.

node_deletions.reason: The pressure condition is not cleanly represented as a single "Low pressure" state in this incident. The truck was pressurized for unloading, while the reaction gases vented from an atmospheric tank. In the current graph this node adds ambiguity and does not materially improve the main causal chain.
node_deletions.evidence: began to pressurize the cargo tank for unloading; released through a 3-inch diameter atmospheric vent

edge_deletions.reason: This is a weak causal link. The cited evidence describes atmospheric venting, but does not directly support "Low pressure" as the driver of offsite dispersion. Dispersion is better explained by gas generation, continuous release, outdoor/low-confinement conditions, and plume behavior.
edge_deletions.evidence: The liquid that was added to the tank and the gases that evolved from the reaction were released through a 3-inch diameter atmospheric vent and an 18-inch lid on the roof of the bulk tank.

issues_summary.description: The current initiating event stops at the hose-to-fill-line misconnection and does not explicitly capture the actual incompatible transfer/mixing in the sodium hypochlorite tank that generated the exothermic reaction and toxic cloud.
C2 as "Low pressure" is ambiguous for this case because the unloading truck was pressurized while the release from the bulk tank vented atmospherically.
The edge C2 -> C11 is weak because the pressure evidence does not directly explain the dispersion outcome.
H1 evidence is not presented as a direct verbatim quote, which does not comply with the schema evidence rule.
